articles.title: Tumours and tumour-like acetabular lesions: the largest cohort from a single tertiary care centre with insights into disease distribution.
articles.authors: Spalkit S, Uldin H, Nischal N, Kaur D, Vaiyapuri S, Botchu R
articles.population: Patients with histologically confirmed acetabular tumours at a single tertiary care centre
articles.outcomes: Age and gender distribution of acetabular tumour types; most common tumours by age group
articles.take_home: In patients aged 40 and over, cancer that has spread from elsewhere (most often breast, kidney or lung) is most common, whilst in younger patients, Ewing's sarcoma is the most common cancer affecting the hip socket. Understanding which tumours occur in different age groups can help doctors diagnose acetabular tumours more accurately.

articles.title: Patterns of wear, fracture, and re-revision in ceramic-on-ceramic total hip arthroplasty: a 31-year retrieval study.
articles.authors: Blakeney WG, Jeyaraj RS, Kop AM, Beaver RJ, Pabbruwe M
articles.population: Patients who had ceramic-on-ceramic total hip replacements revised between 1989 and 2021
articles.outcomes: Reasons for revision (aseptic loosening, pain, ceramic fracture, infection, instability); fracture location and patterns; wear characteristics; factors associated with ceramic fracture
articles.take_home: Ceramic-on-ceramic hip replacements most commonly needed revision due to loosening or pain, with ceramic fractures occurring in about 18% of cases. Fractures were more common in very active patients and in smaller implants, but newer ceramic materials and larger head sizes showed lower fracture rates.

articles.title: Stratified Diagnostic Thresholds by Infection Chronicity Resolve the Controversy in Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty Periprosthetic Joint Infection: A Prospective Study.
articles.authors: Zhang Z, Huang Q, Lin L, Cai Y, Huang Z, Zhang C, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision surgery for unicompartmental knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 77 patients (20 with acute infection, 19 with chronic infection, 38 without infection)
articles.outcomes: Diagnostic accuracy of synovial fluid markers (white blood cell count, neutrophil percentage, and NGAL) for detecting periprosthetic joint infection, stratified by infection chronicity
articles.take_home: The study found that the best thresholds for diagnosing infection after a partial knee replacement differ depending on whether the infection is recent or long-standing, with a newer marker called NGAL showing particularly good performance. However, the authors emphasise these findings are preliminary and need larger studies before being used routinely in clinical practice.

articles.title: There is a Marked Temporal Variation in the Level of Serological Markers Used for Diagnosis of Periprosthetic Joint Infection.
articles.authors: Yilmaz MK, Abbaszadeh A, Cooper AM, Sukhonthamarn K, Restrepo C, Parvizi J
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision arthroplasty surgery
articles.outcomes: Temporal variation in erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP) measurements over time before revision surgery
articles.take_home: Blood markers used to diagnose joint infections around artificial joints change significantly over time in individual patients, with ESR increasing by about 6% per day when initially low and CRP decreasing by about 5% per day when initially high. These changes mean that test results can move above or below the thresholds used for diagnosis, which could affect how accurately doctors identify joint infections.

articles.title: Complications and Failures following Extensor Mechanism Reconstruction in Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Kirchner GJ, Lee D, Rainwater RR, Mears SC, Stambough JB, Stronach BM
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision total knee arthroplasty with or without periprosthetic joint infection
articles.outcomes: Wound dehiscence, debridement, skin grafting, flap procedures, amputation and fusion at 2 years
articles.take_home: Patients who had extensor mechanism reconstruction during revision knee replacement surgery had higher rates of wound complications and amputation, particularly in those without infection. The increased risk appears linked to the additional soft tissue procedures needed during the reconstruction.

articles.title: Expert clinical consensus on the application of vancomycin graft presoaking in anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction : a modified Delphi study.
articles.authors: Balachandar V, Thiagarajah SV, Nyangoma S, Kinagi K, Maley A, Martin FL, et al.
articles.population: UK orthopaedic surgery experts
articles.outcomes: Consensus on vancomycin concentration, graft wrapping method, exposure duration, and irrigation requirements for graft presoaking in anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction
articles.take_home: Experts agreed on how to soak grafts in vancomycin before anterior cruciate ligament surgery, using a concentration of 5 mg/ml and keeping the graft soaked from harvesting until implantation. Most experts were willing to participate in a future trial to test whether this technique actually reduces infection.

articles.title: Does participation in a randomized controlled trial of two surgical revision strategies for periprosthetic joint infection influence surgeons' practice?
articles.authors: Platt NA, Palmer C, Whitehouse MR, Blom AW, Moore AJ
articles.study_type: Survey of surgeons participating in a randomized controlled trial
articles.population: Surgeons who recruited patients to the INFORM trial of revision surgery for hip joint infections
articles.outcomes: Changes in surgeons' confidence, opinions, and willingness to offer single-stage revision surgery for periprosthetic joint infection
articles.take_home: Surgeons who took part in the INFORM trial reported increased confidence and willingness to consider single-stage revision surgery for hip joint infections, even before the trial results were published. Simply participating in the trial appeared to influence their clinical thinking and practice.

articles.title: Association Between Quantitatively Assessed Lateral Trochlear Osteophyte Severity and Three-Year Outcomes After Medial Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Yang J, Wang D, Liu Y, Li X, Liu P, Zhang S, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing medial mobile-bearing unicompartmental knee arthroplasty for medial compartment osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: Pain (Visual Analog Scale), Kujala score, Knee Society Score, range of motion at 1- and 3-year follow-up
articles.take_home: Patients with lateral trochlear bone spurs had slightly higher pain scores and lower knee function scores three years after partial knee replacement, but the differences were small and not considered clinically meaningful. Over 95% of patients in all groups improved significantly after surgery regardless of bone spur severity.

articles.title: Outcomes in Men versus Women After Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Rather S, Green C, Semrad K, Mangan J, Fischer D, van den Anker S, et al.
articles.population: Adults undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcome measures, complications, infection rates, reoperation rates, revision rates, satisfaction, pain and functional performance
articles.take_home: Men and women have small differences in outcomes after knee replacement surgery, with men reporting slightly higher satisfaction scores but women showing greater improvement over time. These differences are often not clinically meaningful and may reflect differences in how unwell patients were before surgery rather than their sex.

articles.title: Intra-Articular Injection Into a Nonoperative Joint Within 90 Days Before Total Knee Arthroplasty is Associated With Increased Revision.
articles.authors: Liao GY, Chansky H, Manner PA, Fernando ND, Tang JE, Hernandez NM
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national administrative database
articles.population: Patients undergoing isolated primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 1,074,331 patients (5,419 received nonoperative joint injection within 90 days before surgery)
articles.outcomes: All-cause revision at 90 days, six months, and one year; etiology-specific revision including periprosthetic joint infection, mechanical loosening, instability, and periprosthetic fracture
articles.take_home: Patients who had intra-articular injections into a different joint (not the knee being operated on) within 90 days before knee replacement surgery had a higher risk of needing revision surgery, particularly due to infection. The reason for this increased risk is not yet understood.

articles.title: Where does your allograft tissue come from? Allograft use in reconstructive orthopaedic surgery: A review of the NHSBT provision of musculoskeletal allografts in the UK.
articles.authors: Telford J, Cornish E, Spalding T, Barkatali B
articles.population: UK orthopaedic surgery patients receiving musculoskeletal allografts
articles.outcomes: Description of NHSBT protocols for allograft donor selection, harvesting, processing, sterilisation, storage and distribution; disease transmission risk; biomechanical properties retention
articles.take_home: The NHS Blood and Transplant tissue bank in Liverpool provides musculoskeletal allografts for reconstructive knee surgery through tightly regulated processes that ensure the tissue remains strong and safe from disease transmission. The review explains how allografts are sourced, prepared and distributed to hospitals across the UK.

articles.title: Mid-term outcomes of medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction using suture tape in paediatric and adolescent population: a case series.
articles.authors: Youssef K, Vampertzis T, Gangadharan R, Rad D, Bailey M, Wadia F
articles.population: Children and adolescents with recurrent patellar instability
articles.outcomes: Paediatric International Knee Documentation Committee (Pedi-IKDC) score, recurrent instability, extensor lag, complications
articles.take_home: Suture tape MPFL reconstruction significantly improved knee function scores in young people with recurrent patellar instability, with low rates of recurrent instability (6.5%) and no growth plate complications. Most patients experienced temporary weakness in the leg after surgery that resolved with physiotherapy, making this a safe graft-free surgical option for children and adolescents.

articles.title: Patient, surgeon, and institutional variation in implant selection at first-time aseptic revision knee arthroplasty: a registry-based study from the National Joint Registry for England, Wales, Northern Ireland, the Isle of Man, and the Channel Islands.
articles.authors: Tyas B, Hewitt C, Deehan D, Baker P
articles.population: Patients undergoing first-time aseptic revision knee replacement in England, Wales, Northern Ireland, Isle of Man, Guernsey, and Jersey
articles.outcomes: Use of metaphyseal fixation devices, hinged constructs, intramedullary stem fixation, and mobile-bearing implants
articles.take_home: The choice of implant during revision knee replacement surgery varies considerably between surgeons and hospitals, with use of newer fixation devices increasing over time. Surgeon experience and the reason for revision influenced choices, but most of the variation could not be explained by patient or surgeon factors, suggesting clearer guidance is needed.

articles.title: Timing of First Postoperative Follow-Up Visit Is Not Associated with Three-Month Patient-Reported Outcomes After Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Propensity-Weighted Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Omran K, Wixted C, Waren D, Rozell JC, Schwarzkopf R
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with propensity weighting
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee replacement for osteoarthritis at a tertiary academic centre
articles.sample_size: 1,068 patients (244 at two weeks, 440 at three weeks, 384 at four or more weeks)
articles.outcomes: Three-month Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score for Joint Replacement (KOOS-JR)
articles.take_home: The timing of the first follow-up visit after knee replacement, whether at two, three or four or more weeks, made no meaningful difference to patient-reported outcomes at three months. This suggests that follow-up appointments can be scheduled based on convenience and patient preference rather than a strict timeline in the early recovery period.

articles.title: The 10- Year Clinical and Radiographic Outcomes of a Vitamin E-Infused Highly Cross-Linked Polyethylene Cup in Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Multicenter Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Afghanyar Y, Beck M, de Gast A, Schmitz F, Becker R, Dominkus M, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty with vitamin E-infused highly cross-linked polyethylene cups
articles.sample_size: 675 hips in 613 patients across nine centres in six countries
articles.outcomes: 10-year implant survivorship (98.7%), revision rates (0.5%), Harris Hip Score improvement, pain reduction, radiographic findings including lucent lines (12.8%) and osteolysis (3.2%)
articles.take_home: This hip implant using vitamin E-treated polyethylene had very good long-term results at 10 years, with only 3 out of 675 implants needing revision surgery. Patients reported significant pain relief and high satisfaction, with minimal bone loss seen on X-rays.

articles.title: Isolated Tibial and Both Component Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty for Loosening Have Similar 10-Year Outcomes.
articles.authors: Hayden AC, Bonakdar M, Gonzalez-Bravo AE, Cochrane NH, Mallett KE, Bedard NA, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with propensity-score matching
articles.population: Patients undergoing isolated tibial revision or both-component revision total knee arthroplasty for aseptic loosening
articles.sample_size: 112 isolated tibial revisions matched 1:1 to 74 both-component revisions (74 pairs analysed)
articles.outcomes: 10-year implant survivorship free from re-revision, re-revision for aseptic loosening, re-revision for instability, any reoperation, and Knee Society Score
articles.take_home: Isolated tibial revision for aseptic loosening had 82% survivorship free from any re-revision at 10 years, with similar outcomes to revising both components. Infection was the most common reason for further surgery in both groups.

articles.title: Under Controlled Femoral Component Rotation, Superficial Medial Collateral Ligament Release Does Not Adversely Affect the Outcomes in Total Knee Arthroplasty for Severe Varus Knee Osteoarthritis.
articles.authors: Kang KS, Huh MH, Kim KT, Lee KJ, Lee J, Mukh AA, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee replacement for severe varus knee osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: 350 knees (104 with superficial medial collateral ligament release, 246 without)
articles.outcomes: Patello-femoral tracking, knee pain and function scores (KOOS), joint awareness (Forgotten Joint Score-12), range of motion, and femoral component rotation
articles.take_home: Releasing the superficial medial collateral ligament during knee replacement for severe knock-knees does not harm kneecap tracking or overall function when the implant is correctly aligned. Patients needing this release had stiffer knees and more severe varus deformity before surgery.

articles.title: Xa Inhibitors Are Associated with an Increased Risk of Manipulation after Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty Compared to Aspirin in a Contemporary Cohort.
articles.authors: McGee AS, Baur AJ, Werth PM, Caprise MA, Duncan ST, Landy DC
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Manipulation under anaesthesia within 90 days of surgery
articles.take_home: Patients taking Xa inhibitors for blood clot prevention after knee replacement were more likely to need manipulation under anaesthesia than those taking aspirin, possibly because Xa inhibitors increased bleeding and swelling. Between the two Xa inhibitors tested, rivaroxaban appeared to have a slightly lower risk than apixaban.

articles.title: Certain Second-Generation Antipsychotics Increase Risk of Complications Following Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Jowkar N, Ruffner M, Koltenyuk V, Chmait H, Sokolik ID, Horsley H, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national database
articles.population: Adults undergoing primary total hip replacement
articles.outcomes: Revision hip replacement within two years, periprosthetic fracture, surgical site infection, and all-cause mortality
articles.take_home: Patients taking certain antipsychotic medications in the year before hip replacement had higher rates of needing revision surgery, fractures around the implant, infection, and death within two years. The study suggests doctors should review these medications before surgery and monitor patients more closely afterwards.

articles.title: Defining the Patient Acceptable Symptom State for the 12-Item Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score at One Year After Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Sandhu K, Lyons MC, Roe JP, Gooden BR, O'Sullivan MD, Carmody D, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty for osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: Patient acceptable symptom state thresholds for the 12-item Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (KOOS-12) and its subscales at one year after surgery
articles.take_home: The study identified target scores on the KOOS-12 that represent a good outcome after knee replacement, with an overall score of 76 representing acceptable symptom state. These benchmarks can help clinicians and patients understand whether knee replacement has been successful.

articles.title: Posterior tibial slope measurements remain accurate only within +/-5 degrees of tibial rotation: A cadaveric computed tomography-radiograph study.
articles.authors: Jasina A, Hinz M, Graber S, Klinder A, Schulz T, Knoop A, et al.
articles.population: Cadaveric knees
articles.outcomes: Accuracy of posterior tibial slope measurements on lateral knee radiographs at different degrees of tibial rotation, with assessment of radiographic quality parameters including fibular visibility and proximal tibiofibular gap sign
articles.take_home: Measurements of posterior tibial slope on knee X-rays are only reliable when the tibia is rotated by 5 degrees or less from the ideal position; larger rotations introduce errors that make the measurements unreliable. Using specific landmarks on the X-ray can help radiologists identify whether the image quality is good enough for accurate measurement.

articles.title: Bone-patellar tendon-bone and quadriceps tendon autografts are associated with a higher 1-year risk of thigh muscle injury after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction in competitive male athletes: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Pecci J, Kotsifaki R, Getgood A, Whiteley R
articles.population: Competitive male athletes in pivoting sports who had anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction
articles.outcomes: MRI-confirmed thigh muscle injuries within 12 months after discharge from rehabilitation
articles.take_home: Athletes who received grafts from the thigh extensor muscles (bone-patellar tendon-bone or quadriceps tendon) had a higher rate of thigh muscle injury in the year after surgery compared to those who received hamstring grafts, though the overall injury rates remained low. When looking at individual muscles separately, no single muscle group showed a significantly higher injury risk.

articles.title: Planned extension gap widening is associated with greater intraoperative flexion contracture correction in robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Leal-Blanquet J, Pons-Riverola A, Erquicia JI, Hinarejos P, Torres-Claramunt R, Novillo M, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Intraoperative extension deficit correction achieved through extension gap widening and posterior capsular release; relationship between surgical manoeuvres and final intraoperative extension angle
articles.take_home: Deliberately widening the extension gap during robotic knee replacement surgery significantly improves the correction of knee extension problems, with each additional millimetre of gap widening providing approximately 2.5 to 4.3 degrees of additional correction. This suggests surgeons can more reliably restore full knee extension by planning larger extension gaps as part of a standardised surgical approach.

articles.title: Revisiting the gold standard: why 2-stage revision THA remains relevant for hip PJI: a 10-year experience with excellent infection-free survival.
articles.authors: Noor SS, Ahmed N, Wyatt MC, Khan S, Qureshi MS, Nazeer NZ
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with prospectively collected data
articles.population: Patients undergoing staged revision total hip arthroplasty for hip periprosthetic joint infection
articles.sample_size: 65 patients followed for a mean of 69.3 months
articles.outcomes: Infection-free survival, implant survivorship, functional outcomes (modified Harris Hip Score), complications and reoperations
articles.take_home: Two-stage revision hip replacement for infected prosthetic joints achieved a 97% infection-free success rate with 87.6% implant survival over 10 years. Patients experienced significant improvement in hip function and pain, confirming this remains an effective treatment strategy for this serious complication.

articles.title: Apparent liner-head incongruity on immediate postoperative radiographs after total hip arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Baba S, Kitamura K, Kawano K, Harada S, Hagio S, Sueda R, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty with robotic-arm assistance
articles.outcomes: Presence of apparent liner-head incongruity on immediate postoperative radiographs and subsequent radiographic and clinical follow-up findings
articles.take_home: Apparent misalignment between the liner and head seen on X-rays immediately after hip replacement surgery appears to be temporary and does not indicate a real problem. All cases resolved on their own without further surgery or complications.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of imaging techniques for aseptic loosening in total hip arthroplasty; a systematic review.
articles.authors: Hopman AGM, Blankevoort L, Van Alebeek EHJ, Sierevelt IN, Temmerman OPP, Jamaludin FS, et al.
articles.population: Adult patients with suspected aseptic loosening of total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Diagnostic accuracy of imaging modalities (plain radiography, CT-scans, SPECT/CT, FDG-PET, bone scintigraphy, arthrography, MRI) compared to intraoperative findings
articles.take_home: Current imaging techniques for detecting loose hip replacements have significant weaknesses and no single method can be reliably recommended. Dual-energy CT showed the most promise, but better quality research with blinded surgeons is needed before any technique can be trusted.

articles.title: Treatment strategy for patients with end-stage hip disease and ipsilateral intertrochanteric fracture: 1-stage or 2-stage total hip arthroplasty?
articles.authors: Liu B, Zhang B, Wang Z, Niu Y, Liu S, Li H
articles.population: Patients with end-stage hip disease and ipsilateral intertrochanteric fracture requiring total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Operative time, blood loss, transfusion requirements, fracture reduction quality, Harris Hip Scores, WOMAC scores, radiographic loosening, reoperation rates, periprosthetic fracture, stem malalignment
articles.take_home: Single-stage hip replacement takes longer and requires more blood transfusions than two-stage surgery, and the initial fracture reduction is not as good, but both approaches achieve similar results after one year. Two-stage surgery (fixing the fracture first, then replacing the hip later) has a higher risk of complications during the second operation, such as fractures around the new hip replacement.

articles.title: From Priority Questions to Registry-Nested Trials: An AJRR-C Road Map for Advancing Arthroplasty Research.
articles.authors: Bedard NA, Hannon CP, Springer BD, Huddleston JI 3rd, Kremers HM, Lewallen DG, et al.
articles.population: Orthopaedic surgeons, researchers, methodologists and artificial intelligence experts from major hip and knee surgery societies
articles.outcomes: Establishment of a coordinated pathway to identify high-priority arthroplasty research questions and develop registry-nested trials; identification of priority topics in infection, perioperative management, new technologies, surgical techniques, implants and quality; development of two new randomised trials
articles.take_home: A new collaborative framework has been created to help orthopaedic researchers move from identifying important clinical questions to designing and running multicenter studies using existing registry data. The approach uses different study designs depending on the question, with randomised trials for clear comparisons and observational studies for rare outcomes or long-term follow-up.

articles.title: Risk factor for developing iliopsoas tendinopathy after total hip arthroplasty : a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Romero Padron MA, Darling AJ, Rodriguez AR, Kossoff NR, Millet Herrera JL, Everhart JS
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip replacement
articles.outcomes: Risk factors for iliopsoas tendinopathy after total hip replacement, including acetabular component overhang, anterior cup prominence, cup protrusion, female sex, and secondary osteoarthritis
articles.take_home: Groin pain after hip replacement can be caused by iliopsoas tendinopathy, which occurs in 2 to 21 per cent of patients and is most commonly linked to how the hip replacement component is positioned during surgery, particularly if it sticks out too far. Knowing these risk factors may help surgeons plan operations better and help doctors recognise and treat this problem when it occurs.

articles.title: Homelessness Is Associated With Increased Wound Complications and Revision Following Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Tummala S, Chow K, Tran S, Boyle K, Collett G, Chen AF
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort analysis using national healthcare database
articles.population: Adults undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty, stratified by homelessness status in the six months before surgery
articles.sample_size: 1,582 homeless patients matched with 1,582 non-homeless patients
articles.outcomes: 90-day medical complications (sepsis, surgical site infection, wound dehiscence); 1-year and 2-year surgical outcomes (revision surgery, periprosthetic joint infection, wound dehiscence)
articles.take_home: People experiencing homelessness who had hip replacement surgery had roughly double the risk of wound complications and a 55 to 72 percent higher risk of needing revision surgery over two years, even after accounting for other health conditions. This suggests that housing status should be considered when planning care before and after hip replacement.

articles.title: Mean 6-Year Follow-Up Outcomes of Two-Stage Revision for the Treatment of Fungal Periprosthetic Joint Infection.
articles.authors: Liang Y, Li H, Hao L, Fu J, Chai W, Chen J, et al.
articles.population: Patients with periprosthetic joint infection treated with two-stage revision arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 58 fungal PJI cases and 183 non-fungal PJI cases
articles.outcomes: Treatment success rates, infection-free survival, relapse rates and timing
articles.take_home: Two-stage revision surgery for fungal joint infections around artificial joints has much lower success rates than for non-fungal infections, with only 41% of fungal cases succeeding compared to 87% of non-fungal cases. Fungal infections caused by moulds were especially difficult to treat, with most relapses happening within five years.

articles.title: Proximal Realignment of the Extensor Mechanism During Total Knee Arthroplasty for Chronic Patellar Dislocation in Knee Arthritis: Results at a Median Follow-Up of Four Years.
articles.authors: Li Y, Zhang X, Chen Q, Wulamu W, Yushan N, Cao L
articles.population: Patients with knee arthritis and chronic patellar dislocation undergoing total knee arthroplasty with proximal realignment of the extensor mechanism
articles.outcomes: Complication rates, prosthetic survival, Knee Society Score, range of motion, extension lag, and recurrent patellar dislocation
articles.take_home: Proximal realignment of the extensor mechanism combined with knee replacement for chronic patellar dislocation had acceptable complication rates (14.7%) and good long-term outcomes at four years, with significant improvements in pain, function and knee movement.

articles.title: Narrow Femoral Canals Are Associated with Less Favorable Outcomes in Hartofilakidis Type C High-Riding Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip After Total Hip Arthroplasty: A 5-Year Mean Follow-Up Study.
articles.authors: Xie H, Zhang B, Ma H, Zhou Y, Kong X, Chai W
articles.population: Patients with Hartofilakidis type C high-riding developmental dysplasia of the hip undergoing total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Harris Hip Score, Harris Hip Score function subscores, Trendelenburg sign, radiographic measurements of greater trochanter tip translation and rotation centre-to-trochanter distance
articles.take_home: In patients with severe developmental hip dysplasia having hip replacement, narrow femoral canals prevented complete insertion of the modular stem component in 17% of cases and were associated with worse hip function and more walking difficulties at 5-year follow-up. These patients required more complex surgery and experienced more complications.

articles.title: Accuracy of Published Projections of Hip and Knee Arthroplasty Utilization: A Systematic Review and Forecast-Validation Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Antal ES, Posta A, Bejek Z, Szatmari A, Holnapy G, Stubnya BG
articles.population: Published projections of hip and knee arthroplasty utilization
articles.sample_size: 28 studies in qualitative synthesis; 93 validation pairs from 17 studies in quantitative analysis
articles.outcomes: Predicted-to-observed ratios for arthroplasty projections; accuracy of published forecasts compared to actual utilisation data
articles.take_home: Published projections for hip and knee arthroplasty were generally accurate overall, with predicted numbers matching observed data reasonably well. However, accuracy varied depending on how the analysis was done and whether pandemic years were included.

articles.title: Anterior cruciate ligament injuries in women's professional football: Higher incidence and distinct injury patterns compared to men.
articles.authors: Huber L, Krutsch W, Memmel C, Weber J, Alt V, Szymski D
articles.population: Professional male and female football players in German leagues
articles.sample_size: 459 ACL injuries (177 female, 282 male) across 2016/2017 to 2024/2025 seasons
articles.outcomes: ACL injury incidence rates per 1000 match hours, injury characteristics including contact mechanism and playing surface
articles.take_home: Female professional football players have significantly higher ACL injury rates than male players, particularly in the top division. Female players' injuries are more likely to occur without direct contact or from indirect contact, and more often happen on artificial turf.

articles.title: Intermediate outcomes from the Australian Knee Osteotomy Registry reveal low rates of reoperation and conversion to total knee replacement.
articles.authors: Vertullo C, W-Dahl A, Hoder C, Sattler L, Lewis P
articles.population: Patients undergoing knee osteotomy in Australia, mean age 44.7 years, 75.4% male, 86.4% with osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: 2563 knee osteotomy procedures (2047 primary tibial, 447 primary femoral, 69 reoperations)
articles.outcomes: Reoperation rates, conversion to total knee replacement, comparison of conversion risk between tibial osteotomy and medial unicompartmental knee replacement
articles.take_home: Knee osteotomy had low reoperation rates (2.7%) and low conversion to full knee replacement at intermediate follow-up (1.5% at 6 years, 2.1% at 8 years). In patients under 55 years old with osteoarthritis, tibial osteotomy had a lower risk of needing knee replacement later compared to partial knee replacement.

articles.title: Timing of platelet-rich plasma administration in arthroscopic rotator cuff repair: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
articles.authors: Tareen H, Mostafa OES, Kwapisz A, Barth J, Woodmass J, D'Alessandro P, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
articles.population: Adults undergoing arthroscopic rotator cuff repair
articles.outcomes: Primary outcome: retears on imaging at 6 months or longer. Secondary outcomes: functional scores and complications
articles.take_home: Platelet-rich plasma given during surgery reduces the risk of the repaired tendon tearing again, with about 1 in 8 patients benefiting. However, giving PRP after surgery only did not show the same benefit, and improvements in imaging did not consistently lead to better functional results.

articles.title: Kaplan fiber tenodesis and anterolateral ligament reconstruction provide comparable functional outcomes after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: A propensity score-matched study at a minimum 2-year follow-up.
articles.authors: Brossier C, Pintore A, Vermorel PH, Boyer B, Philippot R, Neri T
articles.study_type: Retrospective comparative study with propensity-score matching from a prospective registry
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with anterolateral augmentation
articles.outcomes: Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (KOOS), International Knee Documentation Committee (IKDC) subjective score, Tegner activity scale, Patient Acceptable Symptom State (PASS), and graft re-rupture rates at minimum 2-year follow-up
articles.take_home: Kaplan fibre tenodesis using the native iliotibial band produces similar functional outcomes to anterolateral ligament reconstruction using a free tendon graft, with comparable graft survival rates. Both techniques can effectively reduce rotational instability after ACL reconstruction.

articles.title: Complications of total hip arthroplasty in patients with ankylosing spondylitis: a meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Chaniotakis C, Kapsetakis P, Kastanis G, Mavrogenis AF, Zampetakis K, Tsioupros A, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty with and without ankylosing spondylitis
articles.outcomes: Postoperative dislocation, periprosthetic joint infection, periprosthetic fracture, and blood transfusion rates
articles.take_home: Patients with ankylosing spondylitis who have hip replacement surgery have higher rates of hip dislocation, bone fractures around the implant, and joint infection compared to patients without ankylosing spondylitis, but similar transfusion requirements.

articles.title: Association between cementless femoral stem geometry and early aseptic loosening following primary total hip arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Chi R, Najdawi JJ, Nakla AP, Burr RG, Rajaee SS
articles.population: Patients aged 65 years and older undergoing cementless primary total hip arthroplasty for osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: 2952 procedures (1000 single-taper, 1185 collarless dual/triple-taper, 213 collared dual/triple-taper, 554 fit-and-fill stems)
articles.outcomes: 2-year rates of femoral aseptic loosening and return to operating room
articles.take_home: Single-taper femoral stems had higher rates of loosening and need for further surgery within 2 years compared to other stem designs. Surgeons should consider alternative stem designs for older patients having hip replacement without cement.

articles.title: Conversion hip arthroplasty has a higher risk of venous thromboembolism disease at 30 days than primary total hip arthroplasty and revision total hip arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Chakraborty A, Pasternak T, Brown NM
articles.study_type: Retrospective cross-sectional analysis using national surgical database
articles.population: Adult patients undergoing primary, conversion, or revision total hip arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 475,002 patients (primary THA: 428,245; conversion THA: 10,637; revision THA: 36,120)
articles.outcomes: 30-day postoperative deep vein thrombosis (DVT) rates across the three procedure types
articles.take_home: Conversion hip replacement surgery has a higher risk of blood clots in the legs within 30 days after surgery compared with primary or revision hip replacement. Older age, longer operating time, and chronic steroid use were also found to increase the risk of blood clots.

articles.title: Collateral Adverse Outcomes in Orthopaedic Surgery.
articles.authors: Nguyen KT, Yamanouchi K, Bansal A, Daniels AH, Louie PK
articles.study_type: Review article defining collateral adverse outcomes in orthopaedic surgery
articles.population: Orthopaedic surgery patients across all subspecialties
articles.outcomes: Collateral adverse outcomes (CAOs) defined as expected, procedure-inherent sequelae of technically sound surgery; examples include dysphagia after anterior cervical spine surgery, donor-site morbidity after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction, and kneeling difficulty after total knee arthroplasty
articles.take_home: Some unwanted effects after orthopaedic surgery are expected and inherent to the procedure itself rather than errors, and cannot be completely prevented. Clear conversation with patients before surgery about what to expect is the most effective way to manage these outcomes.

articles.title: Beyond sacral slope change: a new lumbar flexion-based hip-spine classification for total hip arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Shafiei SH, Bromwich L, Plaskos C, Bare J, McMahon S, Carr A, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 1,795 primary THA cases in 1,673 patients, mean age 66.1 years
articles.outcomes: Dislocation rates, Hip User Index scores, spinopelvic risk factor prevalence, comparison of classification systems
articles.take_home: A new classification system based on actual lumbar bending ability identifies patients at risk of hip dislocation more accurately than the previous method that relied on sacral slope change. This more precise approach could help surgeons plan better individualised treatment and potentially reduce hip dislocation complications.

articles.title: Debridement, Antibiotics, and Implant Retention for Periprosthetic Joint Infection Following Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Outcomes and Predictors of Failure.
articles.authors: Dowling J, O'Grady J, Howie E
articles.population: Adults with periprosthetic joint infection after unicompartmental knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 206 patients with infection, 175 treated with debridement, antibiotics, and implant retention
articles.outcomes: Infection eradication rate and predictors of failure; secondary outcome of conversion to total knee arthroplasty
articles.take_home: Debridement, antibiotics, and implant retention successfully cleared the infection in approximately 72% of patients, but about one in four needed further surgery. The treatment appeared to work better for acute infections, though evidence quality was very low.

articles.title: The Effects of Non-Psoriatic Dermatitis on Total Hip Arthroplasty Outcomes: A Propensity-Matched Analysis with Longitudinal Follow-Up.
articles.authors: Nagarajan P, Nagarajan S, Brown NM
articles.study_type: Propensity-matched cohort study with longitudinal follow-up
articles.population: Patients aged 18 years or older undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty between 2003 and 2020
articles.outcomes: Emergency department admission, periprosthetic dislocation or instability, inpatient readmission, deep vein thrombosis, falls, and periprosthetic fracture at 90 days, one year, and two years post-operatively
articles.take_home: Non-psoriatic dermatitis alone was not associated with increased complications after hip replacement surgery beyond 90 days. However, patients with non-psoriatic dermatitis who were taking medications for it had higher rates of blood clots, falls, and fractures near the implant up to two years after surgery.

articles.title: Worse Fixation of Cemented Patellar Components on Magnetic Resonance Imaging is Associated with Increased Patellar Component Surface Damage.
articles.authors: Hwang R, Sacher SE, Shenoy AA, Potter HG, Wright TM, Padgett DE
articles.study_type: Retrospective analysis of revised patellar components
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision surgery for cemented patellar components
articles.sample_size: 122 cemented all-polyethylene patellar components (32 from infection, 90 from aseptic revision)
articles.outcomes: Patellar component surface damage measured by Hood scoring system; bone-cement integration assessed on MRI; association between poor fixation and surface damage
articles.take_home: Patellar implants with poor bone-cement integration seen on MRI scans showed significantly more surface wear and damage. Poor fixation and increased wear were associated with component loosening, suggesting that the two problems are linked.

articles.title: Monoflange Versus Multiflange: Custom-Made Acetabular Implants in Revision Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Babasiz M, Zellner AA, Babasiz T, Assaf E, Froschen FS, Strauss AC, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision total hip arthroplasty with severe acetabular bone loss treated with custom-made acetabular components
articles.sample_size: 154 custom-made acetabular components (101 monoflange and 53 multiflange)
articles.outcomes: Clinical outcomes (Oxford Hip Score), radiographic findings, complications, implant survival, revision procedures, hospital stay, blood loss, operative time, osseointegration rates, periprosthetic joint infection rates, center of rotation restoration
articles.take_home: Monoflange custom-made hip implants showed better short-term outcomes than multiflange designs, including shorter surgery times, less blood loss, better bone integration, and lower risk of needing implant removal. However, the multiflange implants had been followed for longer on average, so these results need confirming in future studies.

articles.title: Can Outpatient Total Hip Arthroplasty Be Done at a Complex, Academic, Quaternary Referral Center?
articles.authors: Valtanen RS, Mavrommatis S, Ommen J, Hannon CP, Bedard NA, Sierra RJ, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing same-day discharge primary total hip replacement at an academic quaternary referral centre
articles.sample_size: 1,970 outpatient primary hip replacements in 1,813 unique patients between 2019 and 2024
articles.outcomes: 90-day emergency room visits (8.6%), reoperations (1.5%), revisions (0.9%), and postoperative contacts (average 9 per patient). Most common ER visit reasons were non-surgical medical issues (39%), dislocation (14%), and suspected blood clots (12%). Higher body mass index was associated with increased risk of reoperation and infection; higher comorbidity scores increased ER visits and dislocation risk.
articles.take_home: Outpatient hip replacement can be safely performed at complex academic centres, with low rates of serious complications, but patients require substantial follow-up contact. Nearly 40% of emergency room visits were unrelated to the surgery itself, suggesting many patients had medical issues that would have occurred anyway.

articles.title: Effect of Patellar Component Downsizing on Patello-Femoral Crepitus and Patellar Tilt Following Simultaneous Bilateral Posterior-Stabilized Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Prospective Randomized Within-Patient Trial.
articles.authors: Pinsornsak P, Susrivaraput C, Surabotsopon P, Pinitchanon P, Boontanapibul K
articles.population: Patients undergoing simultaneous bilateral posterior-stabilized total knee arthroplasty with patellar resurfacing
articles.outcomes: Primary: patellofemoral crepitus at 12 months. Secondary: patellar tilt, abnormal patellar tilt, anterior knee pain, range of motion, Knee Society Knee Score, Feller's Patellar Score, Kujala score, and radiographic parameters
articles.take_home: Using a smaller patellar component increased creaking and clicking sounds and abnormal patellar positioning compared with normal-sized components, without improving pain or function. The study suggests using the largest appropriately-fitting patellar component rather than downsizing.

articles.title: Preoperative Supplementation to Optimize Clinical Outcomes After Total Hip and Knee Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Bensa A, Madrazo-Ibarra A, Soth BT, Andres-Bergos J, Rodeo SA
articles.population: Patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty or total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Length of hospital stay, postoperative blood glucose, muscle preservation, haemoglobin levels, transfusion rates, infection rates
articles.take_home: Carbohydrate loading before hip or knee replacement surgery may shorten hospital stays slightly, and amino acid supplements may help preserve muscle after surgery, but the evidence overall is not strong enough to recommend supplements routinely for all patients having these operations.

articles.title: Higher Doses of Perioperative Dexamethasone are Not Associated with an Increased Risk of Infection Following Total Hip and Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Telang SS, Wier J, Kumaran P, Jones IA, Lim MA, Hannon CP, et al.
articles.study_type: Observational cohort study using national healthcare database
articles.population: Adult patients undergoing primary total knee or hip replacement between 2016 and 2023, stratified by diabetic status
articles.sample_size: 1,483,703 patients (618,654 no dexamethasone, 252,978 low-dose, 481,551 medium-dose, 130,520 high-dose)
articles.outcomes: 90-day risk of periprosthetic joint infection following total knee or hip arthroplasty
articles.take_home: Higher doses of dexamethasone given during hip or knee replacement surgery were not associated with increased infection risk, even in patients with diabetes. The findings suggest that higher perioperative doses of dexamethasone appear safe in medically optimised patients undergoing these procedures.

articles.title: Durability of a Proximally Coated, Dual-Tapered Cementless Femoral Stem Through 20 Years After Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Wagener N, Christensen TH, Bieganowski T, Novikov D, Zuckerman JD, Schwarzkopf R
articles.population: Patients who underwent total hip arthroplasty with a proximally coated, dual-tapered cementless femoral stem
articles.sample_size: 730 THAs in 622 patients; 391 hips with stem-specific follow-up contributing 6,145.4 hip-years
articles.outcomes: Revision-free survival of the femoral stem at 15 and 20 years; causes of late revision and reoperation; freedom from revision of any THA component
articles.take_home: This cementless femoral stem showed very high survival rates, with 98.6% remaining in place at 20 years with no revisions due to loosening. When revisions did occur, they were mostly for other reasons such as fractures or wear of other parts of the hip replacement, rather than problems with the stem itself.

articles.title: Osteoporosis Medication and Implant Outcomes After Hip Arthroplasty for Femoral Neck Fracture.
articles.authors: Kiuttu J, Hamalainen M, Virta LJ, Ohtonen P, Lehenkari P, Valkealahti M
articles.population: Patients treated with hip replacement for fragility femoral neck fracture
articles.outcomes: All-cause implant-related complications, periprosthetic fracture, radiographic aseptic loosening
articles.take_home: Osteoporosis medication used before hip replacement surgery did not affect implant survival or complications. Medication given after surgery showed only a temporary early benefit on bone healing rather than sustained long-term protection.

articles.title: Quantifying the Electronic Medical Record In-basket Notification Burden on Surgeons Who Perform Total Joint Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Stach C, Yarden JA, Schilling PL, Moschetti WE
articles.study_type: Observational study analysing electronic medical record data
articles.population: Arthroplasty surgeons performing total hip or total knee replacement at an academic medical centre
articles.sample_size: 2,997 procedures across 6 surgeons; 79,084 in-basket notifications reviewed
articles.outcomes: Mean number of electronic medical record in-basket notifications per surgical case from initial consultation through 90 days after surgery
articles.take_home: Surgeons performing joint replacement surgery receive an average of 26 electronic notifications per case during the perioperative period, with revision procedures generating significantly more notifications than primary procedures. This clerical burden is uncompensated work that contributes to surgeon workload.

articles.title: The Banff Patellofemoral Instability Instrument 2.0 : structural validity and responsiveness as a patient-centred tool for assessing recovery after medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction.
articles.authors: Sze IN, Kerslake S, Hiemstra LA
articles.study_type: Validation study of a patient-reported outcome measure
articles.population: Patients undergoing medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction
articles.sample_size: 731 patients (828 knees); 526 completed full assessment battery
articles.outcomes: Structural validity, internal consistency, construct validity, floor and ceiling effects, and responsiveness of the Banff Patellofemoral Instability Instrument 2.0 across preoperative baseline, 6, 12, and 24 months postoperatively
articles.take_home: The BPII 2.0 is a reliable and valid questionnaire for measuring how well patients recover after knee ligament reconstruction surgery. Most patients showed the greatest improvement in the first six months after surgery, with ongoing gains in some areas up to two years.

articles.title: After-hours hip fracture surgery-influence on reoperation risk, mortality, and surgical complications: a cohort study of 98,607 patients from the Norwegian Hip Fracture Register.
articles.authors: Boutera AT, Dybvik E, Engesaeter LB, Guy P, Kristensen TB, Leer-Salvesen S, et al.
articles.study_type: Cohort study using prospectively collected registry data
articles.population: Patients aged 65 years and over with hip fracture
articles.outcomes: 1-year reoperation risk, 30-day mortality, and intraoperative complications, stratified by time of surgery (daytime, evening, nighttime)
articles.take_home: Hip fracture surgery performed after regular working hours or at night was not associated with worse outcomes than daytime surgery. Patients having nighttime surgery even had slightly lower 30-day mortality rates.

articles.title: Nonoperative Management Deserves Consideration for Select Patients with Valgus-Impacted Femoral Neck Fractures.
articles.authors: Bishop JA, Goodnough LH
articles.study_type: Review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
articles.population: Patients with valgus-impacted femoral neck fractures
articles.outcomes: Rates of reoperation, implant-related complications, mortality, uneventful healing, and morbidity following delayed arthroplasty
articles.take_home: Nonoperative management can achieve similar healing rates to surgery in carefully selected patients who can protect their weight-bearing, and failed nonoperative treatment can be safely managed with delayed surgery without increased complications. Surgery with arthroplasty carries lower reoperation rates than fixation alone, so treatment should be individualised through shared decision-making.
